search-options.heading: Search options
search-options.open-new-tab: Open result links in a new tab
search-options.open-new-tab-aria: Open result links in a new tab
search-options.inline-gif-playback: Disable GIF animation in image results
search-options.inline-gif-playback-aria: Disable GIF animation in image results
search-options.post-method: Use POST for searches. Breaks streaming.
search-options.post-method-aria: Use POST for searches. Breaks streaming.
search-options.post-method-tooltip: POST and streaming cannot run together
search-options.sticky-sidebar: Pin the results sidebar while scrolling
search-options.sticky-sidebar-aria: Pin the results sidebar while scrolling
search-options.hide-url-params: Hide query parameters in result URLs
search-options.hide-url-params-aria: Hide query parameters in result URLs
search-options.show-result-dates-tooltip: Shows the date an engine reported for a result, when it reported one. Turning this off hides the date entirely.
search-options.engine-origins: Engine badges in the results sidebar
search-options.region-tooltip: Engines that support it favour results and local sites from this country. Engines without regional support ignore it.

sync.heading: Instance defaults
sync.desc: Push this browser's settings as the starting point for new visitors. Whatever they change locally still wins.
sync.reset-confirm: This wipes the settings stored in this browser and puts the instance defaults back. Continue?
sync.reset-desc: Put the instance defaults back on this browser. Anything you changed locally gets overwritten.

install.heading: Install app
install.desc: Add Degoog to your home screen. If the browser never asked, this button tries again. Needs HTTPS, and a browser that actually supports PWAs.

backup.desc: Move this instance somewhere else, or put it back. The file holds every server setting on this tab plus your published visitor defaults, tab order, bang aliases, hand written shortcuts, store repositories, installed extensions and their settings, so treat it like a password. Restoring overwrites whatever the file mentions, clones the repositories it names, installs the extensions it lists, and leaves the rest of this instance alone.
backup.manual-extensions: Extensions you dropped into data/ by hand are not in this file, only the ones the Store installed. Copy those folders over yourself. Their settings are in the backup and apply as soon as the folders are there.
backup.export-too-large: Your settings are too big to fit in one backup file, the server log says by how much
backup.import-confirm: This overwrites the server settings listed in the backup, clones any repository it names, installs the extensions it lists and writes back its shortcut code, which then runs on this server. Then it reloads this page. Cloning can take a while. There is no undo.
backup.imported-partial: Restored {count} settings, but {failed} things did not make it - the server log says which
backup.import-invalid: That file is not a Degoog settings backup
backup.import-empty: That backup holds nothing this build knows about
backup.import-too-large: That backup is bigger than this instance will accept

presets.desc: One click for a common setup. It overwrites the settings listed below. Environment variables and your custom lists stay put.

personal-local.label: Personal / local only
personal-local.desc: One person on a LAN or homelab. Convenience over paranoia, because you trust the network.

private-team.label: Family / semi-lax
private-team.desc: A handful of people you trust, sitting behind auth, a VPN, or a private reverse proxy.

public-web.label: Public web instance
public-web.desc: A public instance with streaming, honeypot, and rate limits that will not immediately melt.

hardened-public.label: Hardened public instance
hardened-public.desc: On the public internet and expecting abuse. Tighter limits, API keys on.

indexer-discovery.label: Indexer / discovery mode
indexer-discovery.desc: Indexer on, results recorded locally, the usual public-instance guards still in place.

compat-low-resource.label: Compatibility / low resource
compat-low-resource.desc: Streaming off. Better for old browsers, buffering proxies, and tiny VPS boxes.

warnings.local-only: Trusted local network only. Do not put this on the public web as-is.
warnings.private-team: Put this behind auth, a VPN, or a reverse proxy. Do not leave admin and settings hanging out.
warnings.public-password: Set DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS in the environment. The UI cannot set it for you.
warnings.public-https: Use HTTPS and a reverse proxy you actually configured, if this is on the public web.
warnings.public-monitor: Watch for abuse. Keep admin and settings off the public path.
warnings.api-key: API keys only help if clients send a valid signed request and nobody else has the key.
warnings.hardened: If traffic is hostile, harden the proxy, the container, and the host. A WAF helps too.
warnings.indexer-storage: The indexer eats disk. Plan storage before you lean on it.
warnings.compat: Without streaming, results arrive all at once. Slower to look at, easier to debug, and some proxies prefer it.

server.valkey-unreachable-body: Degoog can't reach the Valkey server in DEGOOG_VALKEY_URL. If the connection dropped after startup, Degoog keeps retrying and changes made on other instances won't reach this one until it reconnects. If Valkey was never reached, settings and cache changes sync through the data folder instead. One instance works fine like this. Several instances without a shared data folder will drift apart. Check the URL and that Valkey is on the same Docker network. If Valkey was down when Degoog started, restart Degoog once Valkey is back.
server.restart-confirm: This restarts Degoog. In-flight searches get cut off for a few seconds. Continue?
server.cache-desc: Flush cached entries. Search and autocomplete are separate. Extensions can register their own, like wiki or ai-summary.
server.api-key-no-password: Set DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS to view and manage the API key.
server.api-key-desc: Clients sign a nonce with this key. Turn the toggles on to require that nonce on search and suggestion routes.
server.api-key-search-tooltip: Require a valid signed nonce on /api/search, /api/search/stream and /api/search/retry
server.api-key-suggest-tooltip: Require a valid signed nonce on /api/suggest and /api/suggest/opensearch
server.search-options-desc: Streaming, languages, and how engines send results.
server.streaming-desc: Show results as each engine answers, instead of waiting for the slowest one. Experimental.
server.streaming-enable-tooltip: Streaming does not work with POST search
server.languages-desc: Limit the languages in the search dropdown. Off shows all ~90 built-in ones.
server.proxy-desc: Send server-side searches through these proxies. One URL per line. Requests rotate through the list.
server.image-proxy-allow-local-aria: Allow the image proxy to reach local network addresses
server.image-proxy-allow-list-label: Allowed local hosts (one regex per line)
server.image-proxy-allow-list-desc: The image proxy blocks private and local addresses by default. Add regexes for hosts you trust, like a self-hosted Jellyfin. Leave empty to allow every local address, which is a bad idea if you do not mean it.
server.block-client-leaks: Block anything that would leak visitor IPs
server.block-client-leaks-aria: Block anything that would make a visitor's browser contact another site directly
server.block-client-leaks-desc: Stops the browser from loading images, scripts, fonts, frames or connections from any other site, and shows a notice listing what was blocked. Some extensions and built-ins such as !ip and !speedtest will stop working. Off by default, the same things are only reported in the browser console.
server.privacy-policy-desc: Shown to visitors from a "privacy policy" link on the home page. Leave empty to hide the link.
server.privacy-policy-placeholder:
## What this instance keeps

Nothing about you. Searches are sent to engines from this server, not your browser.
server.rate-limit-desc: Cap requests per IP so this instance and the engines behind it do not get hammered.
server.rate-limit-defaults: Defaults: 15 requests per 20s, 150 per 10 min per IP.
server.rate-limit-suggest-defaults: Defaults: 60 requests per 20s, 120 per min per IP.
server.request-body-max-desc: Caps the size of public search, autocomplete and panel requests. Leave empty to use the instance default of 3 MB, or whatever DEGOOG_BODY_SIZE is set to.
server.domain-management-desc: Block, replace, or score domains on every result.
server.domain-block-desc: Hide results from these domains. One per line. Subdomains come along for free. Wrap a line in /slashes/ for regex. You can paste a uBlock Origin filter list. Comments and rules that do not name a domain are ignored.
server.domain-block-regex-help: Regex entries go in /slashes/ and use JavaScript RegExp syntax, no flags. They match the hostname, not the full URL. Example: /(^|\\.)instagram\\.com$/ blocks instagram.com and every subdomain. /^www\\.instagram\\.com$/ blocks only www.instagram.com.
server.domain-block-ui-desc: Lets signed-in people block a domain from the kebab menu on a result. Public and unauthenticated instances hide the menu anyway.
server.domain-replace-desc: Send result links for one site somewhere else, like a privacy friendly frontend. Links are rewritten on every results page before anyone clicks them.
server.domain-replace-ui-desc: Lets signed-in people replace a domain from the kebab menu on a result. Public and unauthenticated instances hide the menu anyway.
server.redirect-gen-bad-link: Paste two full links, like https://golf.happygilmore.com/swing/tips
server.redirect-gen-keep-rest: Keep the rest of the link
server.redirect-gen-mismatch: No rule could be worked out that turns the first link into the second one exactly. Check both links.
server.redirect-rules-desc: Left is what to match, right is what to send it to. A plain domain matches the domain and its subdomains, anything else is treated as a regex. Rules run top to bottom and the first match wins, drag to reorder.
server.redirect-replace-aria: Rule {n}, what to replace it with
server.redirect-kind-domain-tip: Matches this domain and all its subdomains
server.redirect-kind-regex-tip: Regular expression tested against the hostname
server.redirect-empty: No rules yet. Use the builder above or add one by hand.
server.redirect-legacy-note: {count} rule(s) were stored in the old "a -> b" format. They keep working and are shown here as match and replacement. Save to store them in the new format.
server.redirect-unreadable-note: These lines could not be read and will be dropped when you save:
server.redirect-fix-before-save: Fix the highlighted rules before saving.
server.redirect-test-label: Test a link against all rules
server.redirect-test-miss: No rule matches, the link stays as it is
server.redirect-test-invalid: Paste a full link starting with https://
server.redirect-problem-slow-regex: This regex repeats a group that already repeats, like (a+)+, and could freeze searches. Simplify it.
server.redirect-problem-bad-target: This is not a usable address. Use a domain like example.com or a full https:// link.
server.domain-score-desc: Boost or bury domains in ranking. Each row is a domain and an integer. Higher ranks higher, negative ranks lower. Subdomains match automatically.
server.domain-score-ui-desc: Lets signed-in people score a domain from the kebab menu on a result. Public and unauthenticated instances hide the menu anyway.
server.oversized: <too large to render> {lines} entries ({size}). Edit this list directly in data/search/search-lists.json.
server.custom-css-desc: CSS injected on every page, after theme and plugin styles, so it wins. Use !important if a selector still fights you.
server.honeypot-desc: Honeypot links bait crawlers and ban them. The browser check injects a signed CSS token on every page so a real browser has to fetch it.
server.honeypot-ban-duration-desc: How long a banned IP stays blocked. Set to 0 for a permanent ban.
server.honeypot-blocklist-desc: IPs currently banned. Expired ones drop off on the next request. Add an IP here, or unban one below.
server.nojs-desc: A minimal JavaScript-free search page served at /nojs.
server.nojs-css-check-enable: Apply the CSS bot check to no-JS searches
server.nojs-css-check-desc: Text-mode browsers such as lynx and w3m do not load stylesheets and will be banned when this is on. Leave it off unless you are seeing abuse.
server.indexer-desc: Save the results you actually see, then serve them back later as a Degoog engine.
server.searx-enable-desc: Lets you install engines from the SearXNG repository on the engines tab.
server.searx-api-enable-desc: Makes /api/search honour format=json the way SearXNG clients like Open WebUI already send it, and answers them in the SearXNG shape. Requests without that parameter are unchanged.
server.infinite-scroll-enable-desc: Drops previous/next and loads the next page when you hit the bottom.
server.compat-desc: Run engines written for other search engines. Both layers are experimental.
server.4get-enable-desc: Run 4get scrapers as engines. Needs PHP 8.1+ on the server. Adds a 4get button on the engines page.
server.engine-origins-desc: The little icon next to each engine in the results sidebar. Favicons show the site the engine searches, provenance shows whether the engine came from the Store, SearX or 4get. Visitors can pick their own in general settings.

proxy-test.not-enabled: Proxy is not enabled. Enable it and save before testing.
proxy-test.ip-unreachable: Could not reach IP check service. Check your network connection.
proxy-test.unreachable-hint: Could not reach the proxy. Check the URL, and that the proxy is actually running.
proxy-test.match-title: Same IP both ways. The proxy is probably not in the path.
proxy-test.match-hint: Direct and proxy both came back with the same IP, so traffic is probably not leaving through the proxy.
proxy-test.server-error: Server returned {status}. Make sure you are authenticated.

extensions.favicon-order-desc: Degoog tries each provider from top to bottom and uses the first icon it finds. Drag to reorder.
extensions.favicon-degoog-desc: Icons this instance has already saved. Checked before any provider.
extensions.reset-confirm: This replaces your engine choices on this browser with the instance defaults. Continue?
extensions.tabs-desc: Which engines start on, and the order of result tabs.
extensions.exposure-exposed: Browser may contact external services directly
extensions.exposure-safe: Browser requests go through the server
extensions.bang-on-title: {bang} searches only this engine. Click to turn it off.
extensions.bang-off-title: {bang} is off. Click to turn it on.
extensions.bang-only: Off in normal searches, still works with {bang}.
extensions.requires-newer-version: Requires a newer version of Degoog
extensions.no-engines: No engines installed. The {store} tab is where they live.
extensions.no-autocomplete: No autocomplete providers installed. The {store} tab is where they live.
extensions.no-favicon: No favicon providers installed, so results show a placeholder. Add one from the {store} tab.
extensions.restart-required: Restart the server or this extension will not load right.
extensions.compat-restart: Done. The engine list has been refreshed.
extensions.compat-updated: Done. The engine now runs the latest {layer} code.
extensions.compat-types-hint: Other search types this engine answers.
extensions.compat-deps-body: {engine} borrows code from other {layer} engines, so Degoog will also download "{deps}". Those files stay as shared code and never show up as engines of their own. Install it anyway?
extensions.compat-runtime-hint: What this engine needs installed on the server
extensions.compat-runtime-body: {engine} needs something this server does not have: "{packages}". Install it and restart Degoog, otherwise the engine will fail to load. Install it anyway?
extensions.compat-desc: Run engines written for other aggregators by different maintainers.
extensions.compat-intro-searx: {link} is a free internet metasearch engine which aggregates results from various search services and databases. Users are neither tracked nor profiled.
extensions.compat-intro-4get: {link} is a proxy search engine that doesn't suck.
extensions.compat-note-native: Once installed they behave like any other engine. Score, safe search, bangs, proxies and transports all apply.
extensions.compat-note-upstream: Upstream wrote the engine, not Degoog. It can break when the site it scrapes changes.
extensions.compat-note-updates: Files download on demand. Update pulls the latest code from upstream.
extensions.compat-note-needs: Some engines want an API key, or extra software on the server. The list says which.

gate.desc: Settings are locked. Enter the password.
gate.misconfigured: The settings gate points at middleware that is not loaded. Fix the gate setting, or set DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS.
gate.generated-password-note: DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS is not set, so Degoog generated a temporary password for this run. Check the server logs for it. To intentionally disable this gate, set DEGOOG_DANGEROUSLY_NO_PASSWORD=true.

indexer.heading: Degoog Indexer
indexer.desc: Save results you see, then show them again on later searches.
indexer.enable-desc: Stores results on disk and serves them back as a Degoog engine.
indexer.domain-allowlist-desc: One domain per line. If this has anything in it, only those domains get indexed. Empty means everything.
indexer.domain-blocklist-desc: One domain per line. Results from these domains are never indexed.
indexer.word-blocklist-desc: One word per line. If a word appears in a result's title, snippet, or URL, that result is never indexed.
indexer.oversized: <too large to render> {lines} entries ({size}). Edit this list directly in data/indexer/indexer-config.json.
indexer.max-per-search-desc: Only the top results from each search are saved. 0 means no limit.
indexer.max-urls-desc: Upper limit on unique pages kept in your index. 0 means unlimited.
indexer.max-hits-desc: Upper limit on saved results kept in your index. 0 means unlimited.
indexer.max-age-days-desc: Remove indexed results not seen in this many days. 0 means keep forever.
indexer.prune-enabled-desc: Delete the oldest rows when you hit a URL or link cap. Does nothing if both caps are 0.
indexer.fuzzy-enabled-desc: Near-misses of past queries can still bring back pages you have seen.
indexer.query-limit: Results shown per search from your index
indexer.query-limit-desc: How many results your index can add to a single search.
indexer.ranking-window-desc: How many recent sightings count toward ranking. Lower adapts faster. Higher stays steadier.
indexer.favicon-store-desc: Degoog saves icons in the index so repeat searches load them without asking a provider. Turn this off from the Degoog card in the Favicons tab.
indexer.favicon-store-max-age-days-desc: Saved icons older than this are fetched again. Sites with no icon are retried after a day.
indexer.export-modal-desc: Choose the engine type to export.
indexer.export-memory-warning: This browser will not write the download straight to disk, so the whole file sits in memory until it finishes. A large index will kill the tab. Firefox and Safari have no save-file API, and some Chromium browsers switch it off.
indexer.export-insecure-warning: This page is not on HTTPS, so the browser hides the save-file API and the whole download sits in memory until it finishes. A large index will kill the tab. Serve the instance over HTTPS, or open it on localhost.
indexer.import-modal-desc: Import a .db (SQLite) or .sql dump into your current index backend. Select the engine type and pick the file to upload.
indexer.import-missing: Select a type and a file.
indexer.import-processing: Importing. Large files take a while.
indexer.import-done: Done. {urls} URLs and {hits} links imported as type: {type}.
indexer.manage-select-all-aria: Select all indexed results on this page
indexer.clear-modal-desc: This permanently deletes every row in your local index. Type CLEAR to confirm.
indexer.disabled: The indexer is disabled. Enable it under Server settings.

store.desc: Paste a git URL. That repo's engines, plugins, themes, transports and autocomplete show up in the catalog. Set repo-image in package.json if you want a picture next to the URL.
store.empty-repos: No repositories added. Paste a git URL to browse its engines, plugins, themes, transports and autocomplete.
store.install-plugin-message: This plugin will run code on your server. Only install from sources you trust. Continue?
store.remove-repo-message: Remove this repository? You must uninstall any installed items first.

wizard.welcome-body: A short walk through setup. Skip it whenever you like.
wizard.search-body: Type a query and hit enter. After you install engines, this is where results come from.
wizard.goto-settings-body: Settings live behind this icon. Next jumps to the store so you can install an engine.
wizard.store-repos-body: A repository is a git URL full of engines, autocomplete, themes, plugins and transports. Add one and the catalog below fills in. Come back when you find another.
wizard.store-engines-body: Degoog ships with zero engines. Searches return nothing until you install at least one. The catalog below is filtered to engines. Pick the ones you want.
wizard.store-engines-hint: {count} engine(s) installed. At least one is required to continue.
wizard.store-autocomplete-body: Suggestions under the search bar come from an autocomplete provider. None ship by default. The catalog is filtered to those. Install one if you want live suggestions.
wizard.store-themes-body: Themes restyle the whole UI. Install some, or skip and keep the default.
wizard.store-plugins-body: Plugins add commands, slots, middleware, extra routes. They run code on your server, so only install ones you trust.
wizard.store-transports-body: Transports are how Degoog makes outgoing requests: direct, proxy, a custom HTTP client. Install one if the default is not enough.
wizard.engines-body: Turn on the engines you installed, group them, set their options. Whatever is on here runs on every search.
wizard.autocomplete-body: Pick which provider fills the suggestion box. Rich suggestions add thumbnails and descriptions.
wizard.server-body: Rate limits, languages, honeypot, proxy, API key. Defaults are fine for a private box. Come back here if you are putting this on the internet.
wizard.security-body: If strangers can reach this instance, lock it down. Set DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS, or DEGOOG_PUBLIC_INSTANCE=true. With neither, anyone who can load the page can install extensions, and those run code on your server.
wizard.done-body: Tour's over. You can run it again from the general tab if you lose your place.
wizard.restart-desc: Start over from the home page: search bar, settings, then the store, engines, and the rest of setup.

natural-language.label: Natural language
natural-language.description: Type the trigger or phrase without ! and the command still runs, with search results underneath.

score.label: Score
score.description: Ranking multiplier for this engine. Higher numbers favour its results.

outgoing-transport.label: Outgoing HTTP client
outgoing-transport.description: Which HTTP client this engine uses for outgoing requests.

timeout.label: Timeout (ms)
timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for this engine before giving up. Leave blank to use the default.

slot-position.label: Position
slot-position.description: Where this slot renders on the page.

slot-search-types.label: Search types
slot-search-types.description: Which result tabs this slot renders on. Images are not supported.

shortcuts.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.desc: Click a shortcut to record a new key combination. Press Escape while recording to cancel.

focus-search.label: Focus search
focus-search.desc: Move the cursor into the search box.

next-tab.label: Next tab
next-tab.desc: Switch to the next results tab.

prev-tab.label: Previous tab
prev-tab.desc: Switch to the previous results tab.

tab-by-number.label: Switch tab by number
tab-by-number.desc: Hold the recorded modifier and press 1-9 to jump to that tab.

go-home.label: Go to home
go-home.desc: Return to the Degoog home page.

result-down.label: Highlight next result
result-down.desc: Move focus to the next result link.

result-up.label: Highlight previous result
result-up.desc: Move focus to the previous result link.

restart.heading: Restart required
restart.modal-intro: These extensions do nothing until the server restarts:
restart.modal-note: Restarting stops Degoog for a few seconds. You can restart later from Settings › Server.

leak-guard.title: Blocked to protect your IP
leak-guard.intro: This instance does not let your browser talk to other sites directly. These requests were stopped:
leak-guard.outro: If an extension added it, disable the extension or contact its developer. If it comes from degoog itself, please report it.
leak-guard.console-reported: [degoog] {url} ({kind}) was loaded straight from {host}, which exposes your IP address to that host. If an extension added it, disable the extension or contact its developer. If it comes from degoog itself, please report it at {reportUrl}.
leak-guard.console-blocked: [degoog] Blocked {url} ({kind}) from {host} so it could not see your IP address.
leak-guard.continue-hint: Continue anyway lets these through for the rest of this browser session and reloads the page.
leak-guard.webrtc-no-servers: a direct connection that can reveal your IP address

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.error: The privacy policy could not be loaded.

search-image.title: Image search
search-image.refine: Add words to narrow it down
search-image.drop-title: Drop an image to search with it
search-image.drop-hint: Or paste one, or use the lens button
search-image.read-failed: Couldn't read that image, try another one
search-image.crop-hint: Drag the corners, move the box, or draw a new one. Arrow keys move it, Shift and arrows resize it.
